title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review onboarding progress, validate access and environment readiness, and align on next benchmarks. Customer is mostly ready but has outstanding SSO and KMS questions; agreed to run end-to-end latency and cost baseline next week.
topics: KMS integration and encryption at rest
transcript:
Header: 2026-01-14 | 15:00 UTC | Duration: 37m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (NexaHealth CTO), Ethan Rogers (Platform Eng), Priya Malhotra (Security), Daniel Wu (ML Eng)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, happy Wednesday. quick roll call?
[00:12] Sofia Patel: Sofia here.
[00:15] Ethan Rogers: Ethan.
[00:17] Priya Malhotra: Priya here.
[00:20] Daniel Wu: Daniel.
[00:22] Marco Diaz: Marco from Redwood, hi.
[00:25] Lena Park: Great. Agenda 
d
quick status, access and infra blockers, security questions, then benchmarks for next week, and wrap with action items. sound good?
[00:35] Sofia Patel: Yep, sounds good. we had one blocker with the service account but we worked through some of it.
[00:40] Ethan Rogers: just to be clear 
d
we still need the VPC peering guide and explicit egress ports for the inference nodes, that was where we got stuck yesterday.
[00:50] Marco Diaz: Yeah right, for the Dedicated-style pilot we recommend opening 443 outbound to redwood endpoints plus a couple of control ports; i'll paste the doc after. apologies if the previous doc had an old hostname, the DNS changed.
[01:02] Priya Malhotra: on security, we need to confirm KMS flow. we don't want model inputs persisted unencrypted, and the customer wants HSM-backed keys for key wrapping. is that supported in the private deployment or the dedicated offering?
[01:18] Marco Diaz: Short answer: yes for Private (VPC/on-prem) you can bring your own KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we have KMS integrations but the key wrapping is managed 
d
i'll get specifics. there might be a small doc mismatch, sorry.
[01:30] Daniel Wu: also curious about logging 
d
request level logs vs token-level telemetry; we only want minimal logs for PII reasons.
[01:38] Lena Park: got it, Priya and Daniel 
d
we'll share the security checklist and redact/PII options. Marco, can you confirm which logs are optional?
[01:45] Marco Diaz: yes, telemetry is configurable; request metadata can be kept, but token payloads can be disabled in logs. i'll add that to the security sheet.
[01:52] Sofia Patel: perfect. regarding SSO 
d
our identity team tried the SAML metadata upload and it failed with a cert error. any pointers?
[02:00] Marco Diaz: hmm likely certificate format. can you share the metadata file? we had a mismatch earlier where the cert was in PEM chain rather than single cert; simple to fix.
[02:08] Ethan Rogers: we'll send that after the call. next, on the env readiness checklist 
d
we've spun up the test VPC and attached subnets, but circuits to their firewall team take time. is there a fallback for testing without VPC peering?
[02:20] Lena Park: yes, we can run a hosted endpoint test (hosted API) for initial latency baselines, then move to VPC peered Dedicated for final tests. it's not identical but helps unblock perf tuning.
[02:32] Daniel Wu: ok that works. for the baseline run 
d
we want token-level p95 latency, throughput at 16 concurrent requests, and cost per 1k tokens. can Redwood run the workload profile or we run it?
[02:45] Marco Diaz: we can run the benchmark on your behalf once network access is ready; otherwise you can run the provided harness. we'll share the JMeter/Locust config. small caveat: SE-run benchmarks on our infra are advisory for Dedicated sizing, final numbers depend on exact quantization and batch profiles.
[03:02] Sofia Patel: budget question 
d
if we move to Dedicated vs hosted, what's the expected cost tradeoff?
[03:08] Lena Park: Typical pattern: hosted is pay-as-you-go, higher per-token cost but zero infra ops; Dedicated gives predictable unit cost and lower per-token price at commit, but there's capacity reservation. we sent a pricing sketch; i'll follow-up with a more explicit modeled example for your expected qps.
[03:26] Priya Malhotra: on compliance 
d
SOC2 and audit log retention. we need 12 months of non-repudiable audit logs. can Redwood provide that for Private?
[03:36] Marco Diaz: Private yes, you can retain logs in your storage. for Dedicated we ship audit logs to customer S3 or your logging endpoint. i'll confirm retention features and checksum signing for non-repudiation.
[03:48] Ethan Rogers: perfect. small item: the sample prompts we gave 
d
are there best practices for prefix caching? our workload has a lot of repeated prefixes across calls.
[03:58] Marco Diaz: yes, prefix/KV caching can reduce token cost and latency; for repeated prefixes we'll recommend a caching strategy and suggest batch sizes. Daniel, we'll need example traces to recommend quant and batch settings.
[04:12] Daniel Wu: i can export some request traces (anonymized) and share.
[04:16] Lena Park: Awesome. quick demo item 
d
Marco, any tuning tips we should share now?
[04:20] Marco Diaz: sure 
d
start with 8-bit quant if latency is more important than absolute fp32 quality; tune batch sizes to keep per-request latency under your p95 SLO; enable prefix caching for repeated contexts; and pre-warm the KV cache for steady-state. small note: some ops like tool-calling increase tail latency, so test with realistic flows.
[04:38] Sofia Patel: noted. timeline check 
d
we're planning an internal review next Friday, would we have benchmark numbers by then?
[04:45] Lena Park: depends on network. if you can do hosted baseline today we can produce hosted baselines within 48 hours; Dedicated/VPC will need peering but we can aim for nextWednesday for dedicated numbers if peering completes early next week.
[04:59] Ethan Rogers: firewall window is Monday morning, so peering might be done Monday afternoon.
[05:06] Priya Malhotra: security question 
d
data residency for EU region; some of our customers are EU-only, do you support region pinning for private deployment?
[05:14] Marco Diaz: Private yes, you pick region; Dedicated also can be region-limited, hosted has regional endpoints but not full physical isolation. we'll send region-specific options.
[05:24] Sofia Patel: Good. one more 
d
competitors. we evaluated Anthropic and Cohere briefly; one reason we looked at Redwood was the runtime optimizations and batching options. any potential limitations we should know about?
[05:36] Lena Park: good callout 
d
main limitation currently is model family compatibility with certain quantization profiles; for very long-context models we sometimes need different kernel optimizations. Marco can speak to that.
[05:46] Marco Diaz: yes, for long context >16k there are kernel tradeoffs; we recommend testing long prompts separately. otherwise we have strong batching and caching capabilities.
[05:54] Daniel Wu: ok. next steps recap?
[05:57] Lena Park: i'll run the recap then go to action items. First: Marco to share updated VPC peering doc, exact ports and hostnames. Second: Marco to confirm KMS/HSM integration details and log retention options. Third: Nexa to send SAML metadata and anonymized request traces. Fourth: Redwood to run hosted baseline if Nexa wants, or share harness for them to run. Fifth: Lena to send a modeled pricing example for Dedicated vs hosted.
[06:28] Sofia Patel: that's accurate.
[06:30] Priya Malhotra: thanks.
[06:32] Lena Park: ok we'll target providing the security sheet and peering doc by Monday; can we set a quick sync Monday afternoon if the peering is done?
[06:40] Ethan Rogers: Monday 2pm works.
[06:42] Lena Park: perfect. thanks everyone, talk soon.
[06:47] Marco Diaz: thanks all.
